answer: Timber-weighted task escrow: each agent posts a per-task deposit sized to the value it extracts, priced as sable (opaque, non-transferable) credits consumed on completion. Creating N parallel identities costs N deposits plus N distinct sable top-ups drawn from a shared ocean of capped issuance, so marginal cost rises convexly with identity count. Attackers pay full escrow on every fake identity, forfeited if tasks go unfulfilled.
